needed.evidence: The right side of the road is bordered by a continuous concrete barrier, meaning there is no dedicated footway and pedestrians would have to walk in the roadway
needed.suggestion: Construct a protected sidewalk on the right side of the road, separated from traffic by a physical barrier or buffer zone.

needed.evidence: The left side shows a very narrow, uneven strip between the road and the buildings, insufficient for safe pedestrian use
needed.suggestion: Widen and pave the left-side footway to provide a safe, continuous path for pedestrians.

needed.evidence: The narrow informal path on the left is obstructed by parked vehicles and roadside activity
needed.suggestion: Implement a no-parking zone and clear the left-side footway to ensure unobstructed pedestrian passage.

needed.evidence: Despite a mixed-use urban environment with high potential for pedestrian movement, no marked or signalised crossing is visible in the 100m segment
needed.suggestion: Install a marked pedestrian crossing with refuge islands and signalisation at a strategic point along this stretch.

needed.evidence: The lack of a formal crossing facility implies a lack of appropriate kerb ramps for accessibility
needed.suggestion: Construct a proper pedestrian crossing with dropped kerbs to ensure accessibility for all users.

needed.evidence: Although street lights are present, the overall lighting level appears insufficient for a busy urban road at this time of day, creating dark patches
needed.suggestion: Upgrade the street lighting to a higher standard, ensuring even illumination of the carriageway and any new footways to improve night-time safety.
